Project under review: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management (a RISC-V bare-metal OS lab, SV39 paging, 2 harts, global kernel lock).
The newly written code is in kernel/mm/mm.c, kernel/sched/sched.c and include/os/mm.h (see `cd /workspace && git diff`).
Everything else in the tree is given/unmodifiable context: init/main.c, arch/riscv/kernel/{entry.S,boot.c,start.S}, arch/riscv/include/pgtable.h, include/os/{sched.h,elf.h,mm.h}, kernel/irq/irq.c, kernel/syscall/syscall.c, drivers/screen.c, test/*.c, tiny_libc/.
Key facts you must verify against the real files rather than assume:
- user ELFs link at 0x10000 but their PT_LOAD segment starts at vaddr 0xf000 (headers included), memsz up to ~0x3e98.
- USER_STACK_ADDR = 0xf00010000, PGDIR_PA = 0x5e000000, kernel window VPN2 = 0x101, KERNEL_MEM_OFFSET = 0xffffffc000000000.
- main.c init_pcb() loads the shell with load_elf(..., get_kva_of) which only WALKS the page table, so init_page_table() must pre-map the code pages.
- main.c's idle loop frees each exited task's kernel stack with free_user_page(kva2pa(kernel_stack_base - PAGE_SIZE)).
- there is no satp switch in entry.S, so scheduler() must do it.
Only report defects in the NEW code. Do not report pre-existing issues in given files unless the new code depends on them incorrectly.

A reviewer claims the following defect in the NEW code. Try hard to REFUTE it by reading the actual files. Default to refuted=true when you cannot demonstrate a concrete failure.

TITLE: Waiters woken by do_kill() re-block on a wait_list that reclaim_pcb() never drains again -> do_waitpid() hangs forever
FILE: /workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c
CLAIM: release_resources() (line 278) drains child->wait_list at kill time, but for a victim running on the other hart do_kill() only sets TASK_KILLED; the victim does not become TASK_ZOMBIE/TASK_EXITED until that hart next enters scheduler(). reclaim_pcb() (line 295) does not touch wait_list, so there is no second wakeup.

Concrete failure: parent P is blocked in do_waitpid(C) on C->wait_list; C runs on hart 1. Hart 0 executes do_kill(C): release_resources wakes P (do_unblock -> ready_queue), then C->status = TASK_KILLED. Hart 0's next scheduler() picks P, P retries the rewound `ecall` (do_waitpid, line 405) and finds C->status == TASK_KILLED, which is neither TASK_ZOMBIE nor TASK_EXITED, so it falls through to `do_block(&P->list, &C->wait_list)` at line 417. Up to a full timer interval later hart 1's scheduler() runs reclaim_pcb(C), which sets ZOMBIE/EXITED but never drains C->wait_list -> P blocks permanently. In AUTO_CLEANUP mode it gets worse: main.c's idle loop then sets C->pid = -1, do_exec reuses the slot and calls `init_list_head(&new_pcb->wait_list)` (line 226), leaving P's list node pointing at a re-initialised head -- a dangling node that will splice garbage into whatever queue touches it next.

content.text:
I verified the claim against the actual sources.

**Key file:** `/workspace/Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management/kernel/sched/sched.c`

What I confirmed:

1. `release_resources()` (sched.c:278-288) is the **only** place in the whole tree that drains a pcb's `wait_list` — `grep -rn wait_list` over the tree yields exactly one drain site (sched.c:306-307), one block site (`do_waitpid`, sched.c:441), one init site per process (`do_exec`, sched.c:228), plus `kernel_pcb[0].wait_list` which is a *different* list (the AUTO-cleanup queue drained by `init/main.c:204-215`).
2. `do_kill()` (sched.c:362-372) calls `release_resources(victim)` **before** deciding the victim's fate, and for `victim->status == TASK_RUNNING` (i.e. live on the other hart) it only sets `TASK_KILLED` and returns. No second drain ever happens: `scheduler()` (sched.c:98-102) and `reclaim_pcb()` (sched.c:295-306) never touch `wait_list`.
3. `do_waitpid()` (sched.c:405) tests only `TASK_ZOMBIE || TASK_EXITED`. `TASK_KILLED` is a distinct enum value (`include/os/sched.h:56-62`), so a parent that retries the rewound `ecall` during the `KILLED`-but-not-yet-reclaimed window falls through to `do_block(..., &child->wait_list)` at sched.c:441 with nothing left to wake it.
4. The window is genuinely open, not theoretical: `arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S:199/157` acquires the global kernel lock only on trap entry and drops it on `ret_from_exception`, so hart 1 keeps running the victim in user mode after hart 0 finishes `do_kill`. Hart 1 only reaches `scheduler()` at its own next timer tick (`kernel/irq/irq.c:105-112`), which is independent of hart 0's. Meanwhile hart 0's own tick can pick the just-unblocked parent out of `ready_queue` first — an ordinary coin flip, not an exotic interleaving.
5. `list_del()` (`include/os/list.h:80-87`) NULLs the node and is idempotent, so the double `list_del` on the dying pcb is harmless — that does not rescue the waiter. And in `AUTO_CLEANUP_ON_EXIT` mode the slot really is recycled (`init/main.c:209` sets `pid = -1`, `do_exec` sched.c:228 re-inits `wait_list`), leaving the parent's node pointing at a re-initialised head; a later `list_del` on that stale node (e.g. `reclaim_pcb` if the parent is itself killed) writes through the head and silently unlinks a legitimate new waiter.

The only mitigating fact I found is reachability in the *shipped* workload: no user program in `test/*.c` actually calls `sys_waitpid` (it is linked into every ELF from `tiny_libc/syscall.c` but never invoked; `test_shell.c` only uses `sys_exec`/`sys_kill`). That limits how likely the default test run trips it, but `SYSCALL_WAITPID` is wired up in `init/main.c:135` and is part of the lab's required API, so this is a real latent hang in the new code, not a false positive.

I could not refute it.
